matches.description: Watch Tottenham vs Coventry highlights and goals from FA Cup on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 16, 1987. On a storied afternoon in the FA Cup , Tottenham Hotspur and Wolverhampton Wanderers locked horns in a contest defined by tactical discipline and late-game drama. With a spot in the next round at stake, both managers looked to their benches to find the spark required to break a stubborn deadlock. Early Drama and Tactical Stalemates The match, held on May 16, 1987 , began with an immediate burst of controversy. Just four minutes into the FA Cup tie, the referee paused play for a lengthy VAR review regarding a potential penalty for Tottenham . While the check ultimately did not result in an early lead, it set a feverish tone for the opening exchanges. Xavi Simons proved to be a persistent threat from set-pieces, swinging in several dangerous corners that tested the Wolverhampton defensive organization, while Pedro Porro attempted to catch Jose Sa off guard with a long-range effort that failed to find the target. Wolverhampton grew into the game as the first half progressed, utilizing the aerial presence of Santiago Bueno , whose header from a Pedro Lima corner was bravely blocked by the Spurs backline. Despite the high stakes of the competition, the first forty-five minutes remained a stalemate, characterized by missed opportunities and a series of goal kicks that illustrated the lack of clinical finishing from both sides. Adam Armstrong saw an offside flag cut short a promising run, leaving the teams level as they headed into the tunnel. Tension Rises in the Second Half The intensity ramped up significantly after the interval. Wolverhampton came out with renewed vigor, with Adam Armstrong and Pedro Lima both searching for a breakthrough early in the second period. However, the game began to descend into a physical battle, marked by a flurry of bookings. The referee was forced to stamp his authority on the match in the 56th minute, issuing yellow cards to both Hugo Bueno and Pedro Porro for dissent as tempers flared on the pitch. In an effort to break the deadlock, the Tottenham coaching staff introduced Joao Palhinha in place of Yves Bissouma just after the hour mark. The tactical shift sought to provide more stability and a different dimension to the midfield. Meanwhile, Wolverhampton looked to their own bench, bringing on Tolu Arokodare to bolster their attacking options. Despite a header from Rodrigo Bentancur that forced a comfortable save from Jose Sa , the match appeared to be heading toward a frustrating conclusion for both sets of supporters. The Decisive Moment The breakthrough finally arrived in the 82nd minute, rewarding the visitors' persistence. Richarlison proved to be the architect of the goal, carving out a chance that allowed Joao Palhinha to ghost into the box. The substitute made no mistake, tapping the ball home with his right foot to send the traveling fans into raptures. It was a simple finish, but one of immense significance in the context of a cagey cup tie. The closing stages were defined by a desperate late charge from Wolverhampton and a series of cynical fouls as Tottenham sought to protect their advantage. Conor Gallagher and Kevin Danso both found themselves in the book for rough challenges, while Joao Gomes followed them shortly after. In the dying seconds of stoppage time, Wolverhampton nearly found an equalizer through a Joao Gomes free kick, but Antonin Kinsky produced a crucial save to ensure the lead remained intact. As the final whistle blew before a crowd of 31,253, the narrow margin proved enough to decide a fiercely contested encounter.
